root_cause.text: In btrfs create_space_info(), the error path incorrectly frees struct btrfs_space_info after btrfs_sysfs_add_space_info_type() has already dropped the kobject and triggered its release callback, causing the same object to be freed twice.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states that on kobject_init_and_add() failure, btrfs_sysfs_add_space_info_type() calls kobject_put(&space_info->kobj) which leads to space_info_release() and kfree(space_info), and the patch changes `if (ret) goto out_free;` to `if (ret) return ret;` specifically to avoid the second `kfree(space_info)` in create_space_info().

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix create_space_info() to return directly when sysfs space-info type registration fails instead of taking the out_free cleanup path.
intent_record.what: The error path after calling btrfs_sysfs_add_space_info_type(space_info) was changed from jumping to the out_free label with goto out_free to immediately returning ret when the call fails.
intent_record.how: On failure of btrfs_sysfs_add_space_info_type(), the function now exits directly instead of executing the cleanup associated with out_free, preventing space_info from being freed on this error path and preserving the object state expected after sysfs registration failure handling.

grouping_result.intent: Fix create_space_info() to return directly when sysfs space-info type registration fails instead of taking the out_free cleanup path.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it alters create_space_info()'s error handling so that after btrfs_sysfs_add_space_info_type() fails, it returns immediately instead of going through out_free and freeing struct btrfs_space_info again after the kobject release path already did so.

candidates.rationale: When btrfs_sysfs_add_space_info_type(space_info) fails, this jumps to the generic cleanup path that frees space_info even though the sysfs helper has already dropped the kobject and triggered release of the same object, leading directly to a double free.

This condition routes sysfs registration failure into the wrong cleanup path; together with the following goto, it causes execution of out_free after ownership/lifetime has already been ended by the sysfs path.

vuln_statements.explanation: On failure of btrfs_sysfs_add_space_info_type(space_info), this jump takes execution to the generic cleanup path that frees space_info. The root cause states the sysfs helper has already dropped the kobject and triggered its release callback, so taking out_free causes the same object to be freed a second time.

This conditional controls the erroneous error-path transition after btrfs_sysfs_add_space_info_type(space_info) fails. By directing that failure into the subsequent 'goto out_free;' path, it contributes to the double free of struct btrfs_space_info.

btrfs: fix memory leaks in create_space_info() error paths

In create_space_info(), the 'space_info' object is allocated
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit a11224a016d6d1d46a4d9b6573244448a80d4d7f
Author: Jiasheng Jiang <jiashengjiangcool@gmail.com>
Date:   Sun Jan 11 19:20:37 2026 +0000

    btrfs: fix memory leaks in create_space_info() error paths
    
    In create_space_info(), the 'space_info' object is allocated at the
    beginning of the function. However, there are two error paths where the
    function returns an error code without freeing the allocated memory:
    
    1. When create_space_info_sub_group() fails in zoned mode.
bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body is sufficient because it includes the relevant error paths in create_space_info(). In this commit version, both failure cases are redirected to a common cleanup path: after create_space_info_sub_group() failure, `if (ret) goto out_free;`, and after `btrfs_sysfs_add_space_info_type(space_info)` failure, `if (ret) goto out_free;`. The cleanup path then does `kfree(space_info);` before returning. Therefore this version does not contain the double-free pattern described in the root cause as stated. Instead, it implements explicit freeing on the error paths, i.e. the fix present in this commit is to avoid leaking `space_info` on those returns by using `out_free:` and `kfree(space_info);`.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it shows the allocation, initialization, the call into sysfs setup, and the error path after that call. The vulnerable construct is present around lines 66-68: `ret = btrfs_sysfs_add_space_info_type(info, space_info);` followed by `if (ret) return ret;`. Per the root cause, `btrfs_sysfs_add_space_info_type()` may already have dropped the kobject and triggered release of `struct btrfs_space_info` on failure. In this version, the function does not contain any protective handling to avoid freeing or otherwise touching an already-released `space_info` on that error path; it simply returns the error. Since the described fix would require correct ownership/error handling around the sysfs add path to prevent double free, and no such fix logic is visible here, this commit still contains the vulnerable behavior and does not yet contain the fix.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable error path is present directly in create_space_info(). After allocating `space_info` with `kzalloc()` and initializing it, the code calls `kobject_init_and_add(&space_info->kobj, &space_info_ktype, info->space_info_kobj, "%s", alloc_name(space_info->flags));`. On failure, it executes `kobject_put(&space_info->kobj);` and returns. Given the stated root cause, once the sysfs/kobject add path has dropped the kobject and invoked the release callback, freeing `struct btrfs_space_info` again would be a double free. This function is the creation path that hands ownership to the kobject machinery, and there is no protective handling here to avoid the problematic free-on-error behavior described in the vulnerability. The fix is not present because there is no adjusted cleanup logic separating kobject-managed lifetime from manual freeing after the sysfs add failure path.
